ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The word aʿrā means to afflict someone.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Hūd's zeal for monotheism makes him interrupt the accusation, disavow the idolaters, and challenge them to harm him without delay.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: his sense of honour for monotheism was roused

MAJAZ:v1p289/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p289/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p289/r7.claim: Iʿtarāka is formed from ʿarawtu and means something afflicted you.
MAJAZ:v1p289/r7.anchor: «إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء» (54) وهو افتعلك من عروته، أي صابك، قال [أبو خراش.

MAJAZ:v1p289/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p289/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p289/r8.claim: Abū Khirāsh’s line uses yaʿrūhu for something afflicting a person.
MAJAZ:v1p289/r8.anchor: تذكر دخلا عندنا وهو فاتك] ... من القوم يعروه اجتراء ومأثم

STUDYQURAN:11:53/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:53/r3.speaker: Kl
STUDYQURAN:11:53/r3.claim: Kl reads the accusation as claiming Hūd was a madman under an idol’s spell because he cursed it and urged the people to stop idol worship.
STUDYQURAN:11:53/r3.anchor: put under a spell by one of their idols, because he had cursed it and had called his people to cease worshipping idols (Kl)

STUDYQURAN:11:53/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:53/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:53/r4.claim: The Makkan idolaters likewise accused Muhammad of madness or possession, as these cited verses attest.
STUDYQURAN:11:53/r4.anchor: The Makkan idolaters, likewise, had accused the Prophet Muhammad of being mad or possessed; see 15:6; 23:70; 34:8; 37:36;

TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r2.claim: Mujahid reports that the accusation meant the idols had afflicted Hud with madness.
TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء} [هود: 54] قال: أصابتك الأوثان بجنون "

TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r3.claim: In another report, Mujahid says they claimed their insult and disparagement of the idols had made Hud mad.
TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء} [هود: 54] قال: سببت آلهتنا وعبتها فأجنتك "

TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says they claimed their gods would make Hud mad.
TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء} [هود: 54] قال: تصيبك آلهتنا بالجنون "

TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r5.claim: Qatada says they explained Hud's censure of their gods by saying the gods had afflicted him with harm.
TAB-FULL:v12p446#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة: " { إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء} [هود: 54] قال: ما يحملك على ذم آلهتنا، إلا أنه أصابك منها سوء "

TAB-FULL:v12p449/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p449/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v12p449/r1.claim: Qatada reports their claim that their gods had inflicted harm on Hud.
TAB-FULL:v12p449/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء} [هود: 54] قال: إنما تصنع هذا بآلهتنا أنها أصابتك بسوء "

TAB-FULL:v12p449/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p449/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن كثير
TAB-FULL:v12p449/r2.claim: Abdullah ibn Kathir says they claimed their gods had afflicted Hud with evil.
TAB-FULL:v12p449/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: " قال عبد الله بن كثير: أصابتك آلهتنا بشر "

TAB-FULL:v12p449/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p449/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v12p449/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says they feared their gods might harm Hud and said they did not wish him to be afflicted.
TAB-FULL:v12p449/r3.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: " {إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء} [هود: 54] يقولون: نخشى أن يصيبك من آلهتنا سوء

TAB-FULL:v12p449/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p449/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v12p449/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says they claimed Hud's mind had become confused because of what their gods had done to him.
TAB-FULL:v12p449/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: " {إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء} [هود: 54] يقولون: اختلط عقلك فأصابك هذا مما صنعت بك آلهتنا "

TAB-FULL:v12p449/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p449/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p449/r5.claim: The verb اعتراك is an iftaʿala form of عراني يعروني, meaning that something struck or affected a person; an anonymous poetic line illustrates the usage.
TAB-FULL:v12p449/r5.anchor: وقوله: {اعتراك} [هود: 54] افتعل، من عراني الشيء يعروني: إذا أصابك، كما قال الشاعر: [البحر الطويل] من القوم يعروه اجتراء ومأثم

TABATABAI:11:53-55/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r3.claim: Al-iʿtirāʾ means to assault or afflict someone.
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r3.anchor: والاعتراء الاعتراض والإصابة يقولون إنما نعتقد في أمرك

TABATABAI:11:53-55/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r4.claim: They claim one of their gods afflicted Hūd with madness for insulting it, leaving him irrational and making his preaching unworthy of attention.
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r4.anchor: إنما نعتقد في أمرك أن بعض آلهتنا أصابك بسوء كالخبل والجنون لشتمك إياها

TABATABAI:11:53-55/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r5.claim: Hūd's declaration of innocence is a performative act, appropriate to renunciation, even though he had been innocent from the beginning.
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r5.anchor: إنشاء وليس بإخبار كما هو المناسب لمقام التبري، ولا ينافي ذلك كونه بريئا من أول أمره

TABATABAI:11:53-55/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r7.claim: Hūd challenges them so they can see that their gods neither harm him nor avenge themselves; their inaction proves the gods are powerless and did not afflict him.
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r7.anchor: ولو كانت آلهة ذات علم وقدرة لقهرته وانتقمت منه لنفسها كما ادعوا أن بعض آلهتهم اعتراه بسوء

TABATABAI:11:53-55/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r9.claim: Hūd calls God to witness to attest that his renunciation is sincere, and calls his people to witness so they can observe their gods' silence and their own inability to retaliate.
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r9.anchor: أما إشهاده الله فليكون تبريه على حقيقته وعن ظهر القلب من غير تزويق ونفاق

TABATABAI:11:53-56/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r2.claim: The response supplies a rational proof against the partners’ divinity: Hūd’s disavowal exposes their false godhood and the claim that one harmed him.
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r2.anchor: مشتمل على حجة عقلية على بطلان ألوهية الشركاء

TABATABAI:11:53-56/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r3.claim: The challenge, followed by Hūd’s remaining unharmed among them, is also a miraculous sign confirming his message.
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r3.anchor: وعلى آية معجزة لصحة رسالة هود عليه السلام

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.claim: ʿĀd were prehistoric Arab inhabitants of the peninsula; their history survives only in unreliable tales, and the extant Torah does not mention them.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.anchor: عاد قوم هود هؤلاء قوم من العرب من بشر ما قبل التاريخ كانوا يسكنون الجزيرة انقطعت أخبارهم وانمحت آثارهم

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.claim: The Quran places ʿĀd after Noah in al-Aḥqāf; the name may be “first ʿĀd,” suggesting a second ʿĀd as well.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.anchor: كانوا قوما يسكنون الأحقاف من شبه جزيرة العرب بعد قوم نوح

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.claim: The people were tall, strong, and physically imposing, with advanced urban life, thriving towns, fertile land, gardens, date palms, and crops.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.anchor: كانت لهم أجساد طويلة وكانوا ذوي بسطة في الخلق أولي قوة وبطش شديد وكان لهم تقدم ورقي في المدينة والحضارة

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.claim: After enjoying God’s bounty, they developed idolatry, built monuments on every rise and grand structures as if to live forever, and obeyed arrogant tyrants.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.anchor: لم يزل القوم يتنعمون بنعمة الله حتى غيروا ما بأنفسهم فتعرقت فيهم الوثنية وبنوا بكل ريع آية يعبثون

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.claim: God sent their kinsman Hūd to call them to truth, worship of God, rejection of idols, justice, and mercy; he admonished them and made the way clear.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.anchor: فبعث الله إليهم أخاهم هودا يدعوهم إلى الحق ويرشدهم إلى أن يعبدوا الله ويرفضوا الأوثان

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.claim: Only a small group believed; most persisted in defiance, called Hūd foolish and mad, and demanded the threatened punishment, to which he replied that its timing belongs to God.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.anchor: وأصر جمهورهم على البغي والعناد، ورموه بالسفه والجنون

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.claim: God sent a barren, furious wind through adverse days, lasting seven nights and eight days; it left the people fallen like hollow palm trunks and destroyed them all but their dwellings.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.anchor: وأرسل إليهم الريح العقيم ما تذر من شيء أتت عليه إلا جعلته كالرميم

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.claim: They first mistook the cloud approaching their valleys for rain, but it was the very calamity they had demanded; God annihilated them and saved Hūd and the believers by His mercy.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.anchor: وكانوا بادئ ما رأوه عارضا مستقبل أوديتهم استبشروا وقالوا عارض ممطرنا وقد أخطأوا بل كان هو الذي استعجلوا به

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.claim: Hūd was from ʿĀd and the second prophet whose struggle against idolatry and suffering for God the Quran narrates; God praises him among the noble messengers.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.anchor: وأما هود عليه السلام فهو من قوم عاد وثاني الأنبياء الذين انتهضوا للدفاع عن الحق ودحض الوثنية ممن ذكر الله قصته وما قاساه

TABRISI:11:50-60/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:50-60/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:50-60/r3.claim: “I'tarāka” derives from “ʿarāhu yaʿrūhu,” meaning that something struck or afflicted him; a poet’s cited line illustrates the usage.
TABRISI:11:50-60/r3.anchor: واعتراك من قولهم عراه يعروه إذا أصابه

TABRISI:11:50-60/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:50-60/r10.speaker: صاحب كتاب كشف الجامع النحوي
TABRISI:11:50-60/r10.claim: The grammarian treats “in” as a negative particle: the people deny saying anything except the claim that an idol afflicted Hud; the exception is from the verbal noun implied by “say,” as in the cited verses.
TABRISI:11:50-60/r10.anchor: قال صاحب كتاب كشف الجامع النحوي إن حرف لحقت نفي

TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid explain the accusation as the people claiming an idol made Hud insane because he insulted and reviled it.

TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r13.claim: Hud calls God to witness and then calls the people to witness his disavowal of their associates, challenging their claim that the idols harmed him.
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r13.anchor: أي وأشهدكم أيضا بعد إشهاد الله

TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r14.claim: He addresses even disbelieving, corrupt people to establish proof against them, not because their testimony is needed; his declaration is warning and excuse.
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r14.anchor: إقامة للحجة عليهم لا لتقوم الحجة بهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#3/r1.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#3/r1.claim: The forms mean something comes over or strikes someone; Ibn al-A'rabi also uses forms of the root for visiting a man to ask a favor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: إذا أتيت رجلا تطلب منه حاجة فقد عروته وعررته واعتريته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، مجاهد، قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#3/r2.claim: They alleged that Hud's criticism of the idols meant one had caused him madness and ruined his mind; this was the general exegetical view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#3/r2.anchor: هذا قول عامة أهل التأويل؛ ابن عباس، والحسن، ومجاهد، وقتادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#3/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#3/r3.claim: Hud answers that if their idols punish him for criticizing them, he will intensify his criticism, certain that they are false and that he is right to disavow and condemn their worship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#3/r3.anchor: فإني الآن أزيد في الطعن أي إني متيقن بطلان ما تقولون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p446/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p446/r1.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p446/r1.claim: Hud calls them to witness though unfit, to establish proof against them, not through them; this is due notice and warning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p446/r1.anchor: قال أهل المعاني (¬5): أشهدهم وليسوا أهلا للشهادة؛ ليقيم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p446/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p446/r2.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p446/r2.claim: Abu Ali analyzes the clause as governed by the second verb, with an omitted first clause, as in 18:96; the preposition with أشهد is omitted before أن.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p446/r2.anchor: وقال أبو علي (¬7): قوله: {أشهد الله واشهدوا أني بريء} على إعمال

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r5.claim: The word means that something afflicted or touched him.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r6.claim: They alleged an idol had made Hud insane and damaged his mind, so that he exposed its faults.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r6.anchor: بجنون فأفسد عقلك، فالذي يظهر من عيبها لما لحق عقلك من التغيير

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r7.claim: Hud says that if they think idols punished him for criticizing them, he will criticize them even more.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r7.anchor: إن كانت عندكم الأصنام أنها عاقبتني لطعني عليها، فإني أزيد الآن في الطعن عليها

ELMALILI:11:53-57/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r2.claim: The people accuse their idols of having struck Hud with an evil that made him mad because he insulted them.
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r2.anchor: ilâhlarımızdan bazısı her hâlde seni bir fenalıkla çarpmış yani onlara dil uzattığından dolayı aklına fenalık getirmiş, delirtmiş.

ELMALILI:11:53-57/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r3.claim: Their “some of our gods” reflects their assigning different specialties and invented names to individual idols, each as a god of some particular matter.
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r3.anchor: “Bazısı” demeleri putlarının her birine başka hâssa isnad ettiklerinden; şu filan husûsun ilâhı, şu falan husûsun ilâhı gibi isimler uydurduklarından dolayıdır.

ELMALILI:11:53-57/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r4.claim: Hud answers their denial and rant by pointing to himself as one of the greatest divine proofs and asking God to witness.
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r4.anchor: bizzat kendisinin[^1] en büyük beyyinât-ı ilâhiyeden olduğunu anlatan şu hakikatlerle cevap vererek

ELMALILI:11:53-57/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r5.claim: Hud calls them to witness that he is wholly innocent of the partners they have invented besides God.
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r5.anchor: siz de şâhid olunuz ki {أَنِّى بَرِىٓءٌۭ مِّمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦ} onun gayrısından sizin uydurduğunuz şeriklerden ben kat‘iyyen berîyim

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r3.claim: They claimed one of their gods had afflicted Hud because he insulted it, so he might have lost his mind.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r3.anchor: Hûd’un, tanrılarına dil uzatmasından dolayı onlardan biri tarafından çarpıldığını, bu sebeple delirmiş olabileceğini ileri sürdüler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r4.claim: In response, Hud called God to witness that he was a true prophet and called his people to witness that he was free of their idolatry.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r4.anchor: Hûd kendisinin hak peygamber olduğuna dair yüce Allah’ı şahit tuttuğu gibi topluluğun şirkinden uzak olduğu konusunda da doğrudan onları şahit gösterdi

BURHAN:v3p336/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p336/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p336/r1.claim: Hud shifts from the statement “I call God to witness” to the command “you witness”: God's testimony affirms monotheism, while addressing the idolaters this way shows disregard for their religion.
BURHAN:v3p336/r1.anchor: ولا شك أن معنى إشهاد الله على البراءة صحيح في معنى يثبت التوحيد بخلاف إشهادهم

ITQAN:v3p233/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p233/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p233/r1.claim: The passage shifts from the past-tense قال to the imperative اشهدوا, an example of changing verbal form within the discourse.
ITQAN:v3p233/r1.anchor: قال إني أشهد الله واشهدوا أني بريء

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#7/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#7/r1.claim: Iʿtarāka means afflicted or struck you with madness; ʿaranī and iʿtarānī describe something that comes upon a person.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#7/r1.anchor: {إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء} أي: أصابك بخبل، يقال: عراني كذا وكذا واعتراني: إذا ألم بي.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#7/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#7/r2.speaker: النابغة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#7/r2.claim: Al-Nābigha's verse uses ʿāriyan for a visitor who comes seeking the host's bounty.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#7/r2.anchor:
ومنه قول النابغة:
أتيتك عاريا خلقا ثيابي ... على خوف تظن بي الظنون (1)

NAHHAS:v2p287/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p287/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p287/r5.claim: Masculine agreement follows the form of بعض; feminine agreement is also possible by meaning.
NAHHAS:v2p287/r5.anchor: على تذكير بعض ويجوز التأنيث على المعنى

SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r1.claim: The clause after إلا is most straightforwardly the quoted content of نقول, as in ما قلت إلا زيد قائم.
SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r1.anchor: الظاهر أن ما بعد " إلا " مفعول بالقول قبله، إذ المراد: إن نقول إلا هذا اللفظ فالجملة محكية نحو قولك: " ما قلت إلا زيد قائم "

SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ instead makes the clause explain an omitted verbal noun or puts it in the accusative as the object of ذكر; al-Samīn rejects these as needless when direct quotation is clear.
SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r2.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " الجملة مفسرة لمصدر محذوف، التقدير: إن نقول إلا قولا هو اعتراك، ويجوز أن يكون موضعها نصبا

SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats اعتراك as the object of نقول and إلا as a redundant, emptied exception particle; al-Samīn explains that as a meaning-based gloss, not the syntactic account.
SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " اعتراك " مفعول " نقول " و " إلا " لغو، أي: ما نقول إلا قولنا " اعتراك "

SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r4.claim: اعترى is form VIII of عرا يعروه, meaning to befall or afflict; it takes two objects, the second through a preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:11:54/r4.anchor: ويقال: اعتراه بكذا يعتريه، وهو افتعل من عراه يعروه إذا أصابه

SAMIN-DURR:11:54#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:54#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:54#2/r1.claim: أني بريء is a case of competing government: أشهد and اشهدوا both seek it, and the second verb governs it, since using the first would require an object pronoun with the second.
SAMIN-DURR:11:54#2/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون من باب الإعمال لأن " أشهد " يطلبه، و " اشهدوا " يطلبه أيضا

SAMIN-DURR:11:54#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:54#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:54#2/r2.claim: ما in مما تشركون may be a verbal noun, your associating partners, or a relative pronoun meaning those whom you make partners.
SAMIN-DURR:11:54#2/r2.anchor: و " مما تشركون " يجوز أن تكون " ما " مصدرية، أي: من إشراككم آلهة من دونه

ZAJJAJ:v3p56/r13.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p56/r13.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p56/r13.claim: The people claimed that one of their idols had touched Hud with madness because he had insulted it.
ZAJJAJ:v3p56/r13.anchor: أي ما نقول إلا مسك بعض أصنامنا بجنون

ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n77/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n77/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n77/r1.claim: Hud's compatriots insinuate that a god has afflicted him with madness.

ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n78/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n78/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n78/r1.claim: Asad also renders the oath as Hud's declaration that he is guiltless of their associating others with God, rejecting their sarcastic madness claim.
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n78/r1.anchor: thus rejecting the sardonic suggestion of his compatriots that one of their imaginary deities might have stricken him with madness

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r3.claim: After they allege that some deity harmed him, Hud disavows their gods and challenges them all; “all” answers their “some.”
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r3.anchor: فزاد كلمة: (جميعاً) زيادة في التحدي رداً على قولهم: {إِن نَّقُولُ إِلاَّ اعتراك بَعْضُ آلِهَتِنَا بسواء}

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.claim: Hud repeatedly uses the first-person yā in this passage, whereas Araf shows it only once, in “Indeed, my protector is Allah”; this repetition suits Hud.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.anchor: ومن ناحية أخرى نرى أنه قد تردد ذكر ياء الضمير في هود في هذا الموطن مرات عديدة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p875/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p875/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p875/r1.claim: Hūd's personal confrontation and threat of harm make “the One who originated me” apt: the one who created him will protect him; the following verse also says God can replace the people.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p875/r1.anchor: فالأمر إذن شخصي وليس عامّاً فاقتضى ذكر (الذي فطرني)

NASHR:v2p169#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p169#2/r1.speaker: نافع، أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p169#2/r1.claim: Nafi and Abu Ja'far open the speaker yāʾ in the ten listed loci, including 11:54 and 27:29; the other loci are in 3:36, 5:29, 5:115, 6:14, 7:156, 28:27 and 39:12.
NASHR:v2p169#2/r1.anchor: ففتح الياء فيهن نافع وأبو جعفر إلا أني أوفي فإنه اختلف فيها عن أبي جعفر

NASHR:v2p292/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p292/r7.speaker: المدنيان
NASHR:v2p292/r7.claim: The Medinan readers open the additive yāʾ in إني أشهد الله.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p304#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p304#5/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p304#5/r1.claim: Qatāda paraphrases the accusation as: nothing makes you insult our gods except that some harm from them has afflicted you.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p304#5/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء ﴾ قال ما يحملك على ذم آلهتنا إلا أنه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p304#5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p304#5/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p304#5/r2.claim: Qatāda relates that a raven was sent to inspect the earth, found a carcass and landed on it; a dove then brought an olive leaf, and received its neck collar and leg bands.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p304#5/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قال ذكرلنا أن الغراب بعث لينظر إلى الأرض فرأى جيفة فوقع عليها فبعثت الحمامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r8.claim: They explain Hud's call to worship Allah alone as madness inflicted by their gods because he insulted them and urged people to abandon their worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r8.anchor: ثم نسبوا ما صدر منه من دعائهم إلى الله وإفراده بالألوهية إلى الخبل والجنون، وأن ذلك مما اعتراه به بعض آلهتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r9.claim: The clause اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء is quoted after نقول and occupies the object position.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r9.anchor: واعتراك جملة محكية بنقول، فهي في موضع المفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r10.claim: Their belief that stone idols can defend themselves and exact vengeance displays extreme foolishness and ignorance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r10.anchor: ودلت على بله شديد وجهل مفرط، حيث اعتقدوا في حجارة أنها تنتصر وتنتقم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r11.claim: Hud's repudiation and challenge, despite facing a united crowd eager to kill him, displays sincerity and confidence in God's promised support and protection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r11.anchor: وعدم تأخره من أعظم الآيات على صدقه وثقته بموعود ربه من النصر له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r13.claim: Hud reinforces his repudiation by the customary practice of securing a declaration through God's testimony and people's testimony.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r13.anchor: ووقفها بما جرت عليه عادة الناس من توثيقهم الأمر بشهادة الله وشهادة العباد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r1.claim: اعتراك means that something befell or came upon him; its root image is approaching his place or side.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r1.anchor: أصله من إعتراه بمعنى قصد عراه أي محله وناحيته

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r2.claim: By evil, they mean madness, accusing Hūd of having lost his reason.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r2.anchor: أرادوا به قاتلهم الله تعالى الجنون

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r3.claim: The indefinite evil can minimize their insolence: they attribute it to only some of their gods, not all.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r3.anchor: قيل : للتقليل كأنهم لم يبالغوا في العتو كما ينبيء عنه نسبة ذلك إلى بعض آلهتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r4.claim: Alternatively, indefiniteness magnifies the harm, implying that only someone afflicted by much evil would speak so irrationally; naming some gods also magnifies their power.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r4.anchor: وقيل : للتكثير إشارة إلى أن ما قاله لا يصدر إلا عمن أصيب بكثير سوء

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r5.claim: The exception is empty after a restrictive construction: the underlying sense is that they say nothing except this statement, with omitted general and specific terms.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r5.anchor: والجملة مقول القول وإلا لغو لأن الإستثناء مفرغ وأصله أن نقول قولا إلا قولنا هذا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r6.claim: An alternative takes اعتراك itself as the excepted item, intended as a quoted word, so no omitted قول is needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r6.anchor: هو المستثنى لأنه أريد به لفظه فلا حاجة إلى تقدير قول بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r7.claim: The accusation explains why Hūd challenged them after they said they would not heed him.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r7.anchor: قيل : بيان سبب ما صدر عن هود عليه السلام بعد ما ذكروا من عدم إلتفاتهم لقوله

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r8.claim: Alternatively, it reinforces their preceding refusals to abandon their gods or believe Hūd.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r8.anchor: وقيل : هو مقرر لما مر من قولهم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r9.claim: Their defiance escalates from disputing his proof, to refusing his command, to rejecting his credibility, and finally portraying him as mad.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82/r9.anchor: سلكوا طريق المخالفة والعناد إلى سبيل الترقي من السيء إلى الأسوأ حيث أخبروا أولا عن عدم مجيئه بالبينة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r1.claim: The lack of a conjunction may show that this sentence is not merely emphatic like the first two, though it still confirms what preceded.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r1.anchor: الإتيان بهذه الجملة غير مقترنة بالعاطف كالجملتين الأوليين يؤيد كونها ليست مسوقة للتأكيد مثلهما

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r2.claim: The objects of their association are things they designate as partners, although God never made them partners or authorized them.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r2.anchor: أي مما أنتم تجعلونه شريكا وهو سبحانه لم يجعله شريكا ولم ينزل به سلطانا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r3.claim: ما is most naturally relative; من دونه attaches to تشركون, since making it circumstantial adds no useful restriction.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r3.anchor: متعلق بتشركون لا حال من فاعله أي تشركون مجاوزين الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r4.speaker: زمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows ما to be either a verbal noun, “your associating gods besides Him,” or a relative, “what you associate as gods besides Him.”
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r4.anchor: فقال : أي من إشراككم آلهة من دونه أو مما تشركونه آلهة من دونه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r5.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r5.claim: Al-Tibi offers a different syntactic account, which al-Alusi considers unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r5.anchor: وللطيبي ما يخالف ذلك وليس بذاك

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r6.claim: أني بريء is governed jointly by أشهد الله and أشهدوا; unlike verbs may share an object if both can govern it.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r6.anchor: متنازع فيه للفعلين قبله وقد يتنازع المختلفان في التعدي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r7.claim: Hūd answers the charge that their gods can harm or benefit: his initial denial of their divinity was implicit in his call to worship God alone, and he now states his disavowal plainly.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r7.anchor: ولما كان ما وقع أولا منه عليه السلام في حقها من كونها بمعزل عن الألوهية إنما وقع في ضمن الأمر بعبادة الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r8.claim: The nominal declaration beginning with أن asserts his longstanding innocence; calling God as witness reinforces it like an oath.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r8.anchor: صرح عليه السلام بالحق وصدع به حيث أخبر ببراءته القديمة عنها بالجملة الإسمية المصدرة بأن وأكد ذلك بأشهد الله فإنه كالقسم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r9.claim: He tells them to hear and witness his disavowal as a taunt, like a man telling an opponent he does not fear to hear his declaration.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r9.anchor: وأمرهم بأن يسمعوا ذلك ويشهدوا به والمقصود منه الإستهانة والإستهزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r10.claim: Some permit coordinating an imperative with a statement; others may supply وأقول. God's witnessing may likewise be performative, or a genuine summons to witness as evidence; the author prefers the figurative reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p82#2/r10.anchor: وعطف الإنشاء على الإخبار جائز عند بعض ومن لم يجوزه قدر قولا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r4.claim: They claim that their gods afflicted Hūd with madness because he opposed and insulted them, treating this as the only explanation for his conduct.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r4.anchor: إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا} أي: أصابك {بسوء} يعني

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r5.claim: Hūd calls God and his people as witnesses that he is free of their association of partners.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r5.anchor: إني أشهد الله} على نفسي، {واشهدوا} يا قوم

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r4.claim: They claim some gods afflicted him with madness for insulting them and turning people away; the root means to be afflicted, and they portray his speech as ravings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r4.anchor: أي أصابك من عراه يعروه إذا أصابه

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r5.claim: The clause is their saying’s content; illā is redundant because the exception is already exhaustive.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r5.anchor: والجملة مقول القول وإلا لغو لأن الاستثناء مفرغ

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r6.claim: Hud calls God and them to witness that he is clear of their association of partners and idols.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r6.anchor: بأن أشهد الله تعالى على براءته من آلهتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r9.claim: Biqāʿī frames an implied question: if Hūd's statement seemed unclear or unjust, what motive would make him oppose his own cousins and closest people?
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r9.anchor: ما ظهر لكم صحته فما تقولون إنه حملني عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r10.claim: The implied question sharpens the puzzle because Hūd's opposition risked alienating his cousins and dearest companions.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r10.anchor: فما تقولون إنه حملني عليه مع أن فيه منابذتكم وأنتم أولاد عمي وأعز الناس علي

BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r11.claim: Iʿtarāka means that something afflicted and enveloped him, sticking to him forcefully like a knot clinging to what contains it.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r11.anchor: فقالوا : { إن نقول إلا اعتراك } اي أصابك وغشيك غشيانا التصق بك التصاق العروة بما هي فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r12.claim: They accuse one of their gods of afflicting Hūd with madness or derangement, which they claim explains his prohibition of idol worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r12.anchor: { بعض آلهتنا بسوء } من نحو الجنون والخبال فذاك الحامل لك على النهي عن عبادتها

BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r13.claim: Human nature fears someone thought to have harmed it and capable of further harm, avoiding words that would displease that person.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r13.anchor: الإنسان يخشى ممن مسه بسوء وهو يتوهم أنه قادر على ضرره

BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r14.claim: Their startling accusation draws the listener's attention to Hūd's answer.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r14.anchor: وكان قولهم محركا للسامع إلى الاستعلام عن حوابه لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r1.claim: Hūd rejects their charge and shows that their gods are nothing, placing the idols with them among the powerless.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r1.anchor: { قال } نافيا لما قالوا مبينا أن آلهتهم لا شيء ضاما لهم معها

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r2.claim: He calls God, the supreme sovereign, as witness to establish his innocence before Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r2.anchor: { إني أشهد الله } أي الملك الأعظم ليقوم عذري عنده

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r3.claim: Out of deference, Hūd does not phrase his words as if equating the people with God; he commands them to witness so their incapacity is exposed and the proof stands against them.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r3.anchor: وعدل أدبا مع الله عن أن يقول : وأشهدكم - لئلا يتوهم تسوية

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r4.claim: The command to witness publicly shows that Hūd considers the people and their religion negligible and expects everyone to recognize it.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r4.anchor: واشهدوا } أي أنتم لتقويم الحجة عليكم لأيكم ويبين عجزكم ويعرف كل أحد

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r5.claim: He disavows the beings they associate with God and stresses their lowliness by saying they are apart from Him, whatever or whoever they are.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r5.anchor: { أني بريء مما تشركون * } وبين سفولها بقوله : { من دونه } كائنا ما كان ومن كان

DURR-FULL:v4p441/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p441/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p441/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the gods supposedly struck Hūd with madness.
DURR-FULL:v4p441/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {إن نقول الا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء} قال: أصابتك بالجنون

DURR-FULL:v4p441/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p441/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p441/r10.claim: Mujāhid likewise says the idols supposedly afflicted Hūd with madness.
DURR-FULL:v4p441/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء} قال: أصابتك الأوثان بجنون

DURR-FULL:v4p443/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p443/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p443/r1.claim: Qatada explains their accusation as saying Hud disparaged their gods because one of them harmed him.
DURR-FULL:v4p443/r1.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في الآية قال: ما يحملك على ذم آلهتنا إلا أنه قد أصابك منها سوء

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says they alleged that their idols had afflicted Hud with madness.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : اعتراك بعض الهتنا بسوء اصابوك الاوثان بجنون

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#2/r2.claim: Qatada says they claimed Hud was acting this way because some of their idols had harmed him.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : ان تقول الا اعتراك بعض الهتنا بسوء قالوا : انما تصنع هذا من اجل ان بعض الهتنا اصابك بسوء

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains Hud's declaration as repudiating the alleged idols and challenging them to inflict even worse harm, since he has disbelieved in them.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046#2/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق قال : اني اشهد الله واشهدوا اني بريء مما تشركون من دونه اي اني قد كفرت بالهتكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r7.claim: Their claim that an idol afflicted Hud is an explanatory resumption: his rejection of their message naturally prompts the question of what they think his preaching is.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r7.anchor: استئناف بياني لأن قولهم : { وما نحن لك بمؤمنين } من شأنه أن يثير للسامع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r8.claim: They attribute Hud's harm to one idol as a threat, implying that their gods together could crush him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r8.anchor: وجعلوا ذلك من فعل بعض الآلهة تهديدا للناس بأنه لو تصدى له جميع الآلهة لدكوه دكا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r1.claim: اعتراء means descending upon or afflicting, and the bāʾ marks accompanying contact: an evil struck him.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r2.claim: They mean their gods afflicted Hud with madness before he began rejecting their worship, for some other reason. This is incoherent sophistry: the gods supposedly provoked someone who then opposed them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r2.anchor: ولا شك أنهم يعنون أن آلهتهم أصابته بمس من قبل أن يقوم بدعوة رفض عبادتها لسبب آخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r3.claim: Here القول means spoken utterance, a form that implies they actually believe what they say.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r4.claim: In response to their rejection, denial of his signs, resolve to worship idols, and praise of their power, Hud calls God to witness that he conveyed the message and they stubbornly denied his signs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r4.anchor: أجابهم هود عليه السلام بأنه يشهد الله عليهم أنه أبلغهم وأنهم كابروا وجحدوا آياته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r5.claim: أشهد الله is a performative act phrased as a report, as are utterances whose effect is not externally visible and familiar contract formulas.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r5.anchor: لأن كل إنشاء لا يظهر أثره في الخلق من شأنه أن يقع بصيغة الخبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r6.claim: Hud calls the people to witness that he disavows their partners, immediately countering their wrong claim; the insertion interrupts his next statement, which continues in 11:57.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r6.anchor: مبادرة بإنكار المنكر وإن كان ذلك قد أتوا به استطرادا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r7.claim: He uses an imperative for their witnessing so that the performative sound of the declaration is not diluted by the flavor of reporting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r7.anchor: لأنه أراد مزاجة إنشاء الإشهاد دون رائحة معنى الإخبار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r8.claim: Calling them to witness makes his disavowal certain and irrevocable, as a matter he has imposed upon himself before witnesses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r8.anchor: تحقيق ذلك وأنه لا يتردد على أمر جازم قد أوجبه المشهود عليه على نفسه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p98/r9.claim: ما is a relative pronoun with its relative clause elided: the sense is the things that they associate with God.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد وثعلب والأزهري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r1.claim: A group including Abu Ubayd, Thalab, and al-Azhari, also attributed to Ibn Abbas, says the seven ahruf are seven Arab dialects distributed through the Qur'an, not optional alternatives for readers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r1.anchor: أنزل مشتملا على سبع لغات من لغات العرب مبثوثة في آيات القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur says the fixed-dialect account does not fit the hadith's context of granting latitude and cannot explain the number, since many tribal dialect words occur in the Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r3.anchor: وهذا الجواب لا يلاقي مساق الحديث من التوسعة ، ولا يستقيم من جهة العدد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r4.speaker: السيوطي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r4.claim: Al-Suyuti, citing Abu Bakr al-Wasiti, says the Qur'an contains words from as many as fifty Arab dialects.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r4.anchor: وأنهاها السيوطي نقلا عن أبي بكر الواسطي إلى خمسين لغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r5.claim: Ibn Ashur favors the view that the seven ahruf are pronunciation variants such as imala, lengthening, shortening, hamza, and easing, granted while preserving Qur'anic wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r5.anchor: وذهب جماعة أن المراد من الأحرف لهجات العرب في كيفيات النطق كالفتح والإمالة ، والمد والقصر ، والهمز والتخفيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur sets aside other weak explanations, noting that some scholars listed as many as thirty-five answers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r6.anchor: وهنالك أجوبة أخرى ضعيفة لا ينبغي للعالم التعريج عليها وقد أنهى بعضهم جملة الأجوبة إلى خمسة وثلاثين جوابا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r9.speaker: الباقلاني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r9.claim: Al-Baqillani had considered that the order of surahs might have resulted from the Companions' judgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r9.anchor: وقد ذكر الباقلاني احتمال أن يكون ترتيب السور من اجتهاد الصحابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r10.claim: The community continued seeking conformity with the Prophet's recitation until Abu Bakr's codex followed the final review; the Companions agreed because the concession's cause had ended.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r10.anchor: حتى كان ترتيب المصحف في زمن أبي بكر على نحو العرضة الأخيرة التي عرضها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأجمع الصحابة في عهد أبي بكر على ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r11.claim: Equating the seven ahruf with the seven famous canonical readings is wrong and contrary to scholarly consensus.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r11.anchor: ومن الناس من يظن المراد بالسبع في الحديث ما يطابق القراءات السبع التي اشتهرت بين أهل فن القراءات ، وذلك غلط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r12.speaker: أبو شامة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r12.claim: Abu Shama says no proof limits readings to seven; the number may have been chosen without intent, for auspiciousness, or to suggest to the public that these are the hadith's seven.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r12.anchor: كما قال أبو شامة : فإن انحصار القراءات في سبع لم يدل عليه دليل ، ولكنه أمر حصل إما بدون قصد أو بقصد التيمن بعدد السبعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r13.speaker: ابن عمار
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r13.claim: Ibn Ammar, quoted by al-Suyuti, criticizes fixing the readings at seven because it confuses the public and says the compiler should have chosen fewer or more.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r13.anchor: ونقل السيوطي عن أبي العباس ابن عمار أنه قال : لقد فعل جاعل عدد القراءات سبعا ما لا ينبغي ، وأشكل به الأمر على العامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r14.speaker: السيوطي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r14.claim: Al-Suyuti says Ibn Jubayr had selected five reading authorities, one for each region receiving an Uthmanic codex.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r14.anchor: وقد صنف ابن جبير المكي وهو قبل ابن مجاهد كتابا في القراءات فاقتصر على خمسة أئمة من كل مصر إماما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r15.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r15.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says Ibn Mujahid first assembled seven readings, initially counting Yaqub before replacing him with al-Kisai; the imams accept Yaqub, Abu Jafar, and Shayba as sound readings too.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r15.anchor: أول من جمع القراءات في سبع ابن مجاهد غير أنه عد قراءة يعقوب سابعا ثم عوضها بقراءة الكسائي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r16.claim: Because reading differences preceded Uthman's standard codex, they did not arise from later judgment about the written wording, apart from dialectal pronunciation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r16.anchor: وإذ قد كان الاختلاف بين القراء سابقا على تدوين المصحف الإمام في زمن عثمان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r17.claim: A reading requires a sound transmission chain even if it matches the codex spelling and Arabic grammar.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r17.anchor: وأما صحة السند الذي تروى به القراءة لتكون مقبولة فهو شرط لا محيد عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r18.speaker: حماد بن الزبرقان
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r18.claim: Al-Zibriqan misread several words, including abahu for iyyahu, ghurratin for izzatin, and yanihi for yughnihi; Ibn Ashur says he had learned from a codex rather than a teacher.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p58/r18.anchor: كما ذكر في المزهر أن حماد بن الزبرقان قرأ ) إلا عن موعدة وعدها أباه ( بالباء الموحدة وإنما هي إياه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r1.claim: People in the Prophetic era sometimes estimated elapsed time by how many verses a reader could recite; a report places the dawn interval after the Prophet’s pre-dawn meal at fifty verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r1.anchor: كان بينه وبين طلوع الفجر مقدار ما يقرأ القارئ خمسين آية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r2.speaker: أبو بكر ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r2.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says fixing verse boundaries is difficult because verses vary in length and may stop before or after a complete meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر ابن العربي وتحديد الآية من معضلات القرآن ، فمن آياته طويل وقصير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari holds that verse boundaries are fixed by transmitted authority.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r4.claim: Ibn Ashur proposes that a verse’s extent may follow the end of its revelation, with the occurrence of a rhyme-like ending as its sign.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r4.anchor: لا يبعد أن يكون تعيين مقدار الآية تبعا لانتهاء نزولها وأمارته وقوع الفاصلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r5.claim: Fawasil are recurring words whose final letters or sounds and spoken forms match or nearly match, making their pattern seem deliberate across many verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r5.anchor: والذي استخلصته أن الفواصل هي الكلمات التي تتماثل في أواخر حروفها أو تتقارب ، مع تماثل أو تقارب صيغ النطق بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r6.claim: Fawasil are judged by similarity in vocalized and unvocalized word forms; they resemble sajʿ and the poetic device of maintaining a pattern beyond what rhyme requires.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r6.anchor: العبرة فيها بتماثل صيغ الكلمات من حركات وسكون وهي أكثر شبها بالتزام ما لا يلزم في القوافي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r7.claim: Every such closing is an ayah ending even when the sentence’s intended point is unfinished there.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r7.anchor: أن تلك الفواصل كلها منتهى آيات ولو كان الكلام الذي تقع فيه لم يتم فيه الغرض المسوق إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r8.claim: When a purpose ends without a fasila, that point is rarely an ayah ending; the opening of Sad is an exception counted as an ayah without a fasila.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r8.anchor: إذا انتهى الغرض المقصود من الكلام ولم تقع عند انتهائه فاصلة لا يكون منتهى الكلام نهاية آية إلا نادرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r9.claim: Some opening-sura endings use an open consonant followed by long alif, while others use an extended final wāw or yā; Ibn Ashur illustrates both patterns.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r9.anchor: فواصل بنيت على حرف مضموم مشبع بواو . أو على حرف مكسور مشبع بياء ساكنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r10.claim: A long passage can remain one ayah when its thought continues to its eventual ending; the passage about David’s judgment is his example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r10.anchor: فهذه الجمل كلها عدت آية واحدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r11.claim: Fawasil contribute to the Qur’an’s inimitability as verbal embellishment and eloquence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r11.anchor: واعلم أن هذه الفواصل من جملة المقصود من الإعجاز لأنها ترجع إلى محسنات الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r12.claim: Pausing at each fasila lets its sound affect listeners and makes them feel the beauty of the patterned wording, as in poetry and sajʿ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r12.anchor: فمن الغرض البلاغي الوقوف عند الفواصل لتقع في الأسماع فتتأثر نفوس السامعين بمحاسن ذلك التماثل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r13.claim: An ayah boundary may divide syntactically connected wording: the cited verses in Ghafir and Hud continue into the next ayah, yet should still be paused at.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r13.anchor: وينبغي الوقف عند نهاية كل آية منها . وقوله تعالى ) واشهدوا أني بريء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r14.claim: Ignoring poetic rhyme endings spoils the poet’s craft and turns poetry into prose; ignoring sajʿ endings likewise wastes a deliberate verbal refinement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r14.anchor: ألا ترى أن من الإضاعة لدقائق الشعر أن يلقيه ملقيه على مسامع الناس دون وقف عند قوافيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r15.claim: The desire to explain meaning does not excuse a reciter from preserving these endings: explaining is a lecturer’s task, not a poem reciter’s task.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r15.anchor: فإن البيان وظيفة ملقي درس لا وظيفة منشد الشعر ، ولو كان هو الشاعر نفسه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r16.speaker: بعضهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r16.claim: Al-Itqan transmits from Abu Amr that some authorities say pausing at the verse endings is Sunnah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r16.anchor: وفي الإتقان عن أبي عمرو قال بعضهم : الوقف على رؤوس الآي سنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r17.speaker: البيهقي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r17.claim: Al-Bayhaqi’s report in Shuʿab al-Iman calls pausing at verse endings preferable even when their syntax connects forward, following the Prophet’s practice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r17.anchor: عن البيهقي في شعب الإيمان : الفضل الوقف على رؤوس الآيات وان تعلقت بما بعدها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r18.speaker: أم سلمة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r18.claim: Abu Dawud reports from Umm Salama that the Prophet recited in verse-by-verse units, pausing after each ayah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r18.anchor: عن أم سلمة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ قطع قراءته آية آية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r19.claim: Reported verse boundaries must be followed, as Ibn al-Arabi and al-Zamakhshari stress, though their transmission does not prevent seeking useful general indicators.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r19.anchor: وجوب اتباع المأثور من تحديد الآي كما قال ابن العربي والزمخشري ولكن ذلك لا يصدنا عن محاولة ضوابط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r20.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r20.claim: Some opening disjoint-letter groups count as verses and others do not, so the proposed indicators admit exceptions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p75/r20.anchor: ولم تعد ألر . ألمر . طس~ . ص~ . ق~ . ن~ . آيات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r5.claim: They claim that some idols afflicted Hūd with madness because he insulted them and misled their worshippers; ʿarā and iʿtarā mean to touch or afflict.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r5.anchor: معناه ما نقول إلا أن بعض الآلهة لما سببتها وضللت عبدتها أصابك بجنون، يقال: عر يعر واعترى يعتري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r6.claim: Hūd openly disowns their idols and challenges them and their idols to plot against him; his challenge is described as a miracle because the numerous, powerful people could not harm him though he stood alone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r6.anchor: فحينئذ جاهرهم هود عليه السلام بالتبري من أوثانهم وحضهم على كيده هم وأصنامهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r1.claim: They claim their idols afflicted Hūd with madness because he insulted them, so his criticism is a consequence of altered reason.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ إن نقول ﴾ أي ما نقول في سبب مخالفتك إيانا إلا أن بعض آلهتنا أصابك بجنون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba says ʿaranī and iʿtarānī mean that something befell or affected me; ʿāʾir can denote a visitor seeking a gift.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة يقال عراني كذا واعتراني إذا ألم بي ومنه قيل لمن أتاك يطلب نائلك عار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r3.speaker: النابغة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r3.claim: Al-Nābigha's verse uses ʿāriyan for someone who has come seeking a gift, illustrating the word's usage.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r3.anchor: ومنه قول النابغة أتيتك عاريا خلقا ثيابي على خوف تظن بي الظنون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r4.speaker: نافع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ vowels the yāʾ in innī.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r5.claim: In response to the claim that the idols punished him for attacking them, Hūd is certain of their defects and his disavowal, and intensifies his criticism.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ إني أشهد الله ﴾ إلى آخر الآية حرك ياء إني نافع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r2.claim: They claim some of their gods afflicted Hud with madness or a defect in his mind because he condemned their worship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r2.anchor: يقولون: ما نظن إلا أن بعض الآلهة أصابك بجنون وخبل في عقلك بسبب نهيك عن عبادتها وعيبك لها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r3.claim: Hud calls God and his people to witness that he is free of every partner and idol they associate with God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r3.anchor: يقول: إني بريء من جميع الأنداد والأصنام

JISHUMI:v5p3513/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r4.claim: The verb اعتراه means that something struck or afflicted someone.
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r4.anchor: اعتراه الشيء: أصابه، يقال عراه الشيء يعروه أصابه

JISHUMI:v5p3513/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r5.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r5.claim: The poet uses تعروني for an affliction that seizes or shakes him at the beloved's remembrance.
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r5.anchor: قال الشاعر: وإني لتعروني لذكراك نفضة ... كما انتفض العصفور بلله القطر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r1.claim: اعتراك is the object of نقول, while إلا is redundant; the charge means they say only that one of their gods has afflicted Hud with madness.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r2.claim: The people allege that their gods made Hud mad because he insulted them, rejected them, and opposed them, as retaliation for his bad conduct.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r2.anchor: أي خبلك ومسك بجنون لسبك إياها وصدك عنها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r3.claim: It is unsurprising that the unbelieving people of ʿĀd call repentance and seeking forgiveness madness; the author condemns Muslims who use the same insult.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r3.anchor: أن يسموا التوبة والاستغفار خبلا وجنونا وهم عاد أعلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r4.claim: He rebukes professing Muslims who call a penitent or one returning to God mad, saying their scant fellowship with such people betrays residual irreligion and heresy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r4.anchor: يسمون التائب من ذنوبه مجنونا والمنيب إلى ربه مخبلا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r5.claim: The people’s earlier replies show them hard-hearted, heedless of advice, untroubled by slander, and unmoved toward right guidance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r5.anchor: على أن القوم كانوا جفاة غلاظ الأكباد ، لا يبالون بالبهت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r6.claim: Their final claim reveals extreme ignorance: they imagine stones can defend themselves and exact revenge; perhaps they also believe such gods can reward.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r6.anchor: اعتقدوا في حجارة أنها تنصر وتنتقم ، ولعلهم حين أجازوا العقاب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r7.claim: Hud's lone confrontation with a bloodthirsty united nation is a great sign of his confidence that God will protect him from them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r7.anchor: من أعظم الآيات أن يواجه بهذا الكلام رجل واحد أمة عطاشا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r8.claim: Hud confirms his disavowal by customary human practice; God's witness establishes monotheism, while addressing them as witnesses scorns their religion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r8.anchor: إشهاد الله على البراءة من الشرك إشهاد صحيح ثابت في معنى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r9.claim: He says اشهدوا rather than أشهدكم because their witness is contemptuous mockery, like telling someone estranged to witness that one does not love him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r9.anchor: اشهد علي أني لا أحبك ، تهكما به واستهانة بحاله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r10.claim: من دونه can mean their associating other gods with God, or the gods they themselves make partners; God did not make them partners or send authority for them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#3/r10.anchor: من إشراككم آلهة من دونه ، أو مما تشركونه من آلهة من دونه

MUJAHID:v1p305#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p305#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p305#3/r1.claim: Mujahid explains the accusation as saying that the idols afflicted Hud with madness.
MUJAHID:v1p305#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء ﴾ قال اصابتك الأوثان بجنون

MUQATIL:11:53-55/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r3.claim: They claim one of their idols afflicted Hud with madness or mental impairment, and say they do not want him harmed, so he should avoid the idols and remain safe.
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r3.anchor: ولا نحب أن يصيبك أو يعتريك ذلك فاجتنبها سالما

MUQATIL:11:53-55/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r4.speaker: الفراء
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r4.claim: Abdullah reports al-Farra's distinction: الخبل with a still bāʾ is an illness that prevents movement and disables the body, while الخبل with a vowel on bāʾ means madness.
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r4.anchor: قال عبد الله: قال الفراء: الخبل مسكنة الباء

MUQATIL:11:53-55/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r5.claim: Hud calls God and the people to witness that he disavows the things they associate with God.
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r5.anchor: قال إني أشهد الله واشهدوا أني بريء مما تشركون

NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#2/r1.claim: In is negative: they deny saying anything except the accusation that Hūd was afflicted.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#2/r1.anchor: إن حرف نفى فنفى جميع القول إلا قولا واحدا وهو قولهم اعتراك

NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#2/r2.claim: They allege that one of their gods struck Hūd with madness or derangement.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#2/r2.anchor: أصابك بعض آلهتنا بسوء بجنون وخبل

NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r2.claim: The command to witness is taunting, like telling someone with whom relations have dried up to witness that one dislikes him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#3/r2.anchor: وجئ به على لفظ الأمر بالشهادة كما يقول الرجل لمن يبس الثرى بينه وبينه اشهد على إنى لا أحبك تهكما به واستهانة بحاله

QURTUBI-FULL:11:50-54/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:50-54/r23.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:50-54/r23.claim: Iʿtarāka means afflicted or came upon you; ʿarāhu and iʿtarāhu mean an event befell him.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:50-54/r23.anchor: قوله تعالى: { إن نقول إلا اعتراك } أي أصابك.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:50-54/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:50-54/r24.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:50-54/r24.claim: Their gods are idols; the evil with which they allegedly afflicted Hūd means madness for insulting them, as Ibn ʿAbbas and others explain.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:50-54/r24.anchor: { بعض آلهتنا } أي أصنامنا. { بسوء } أي بجنون لسبك إياها، عن ابن عباس وغيره.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r1.claim: Hūd calls God to witness concerning himself.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r2.claim: He calls them to witness not because they are qualified witnesses, but to make the declaration emphatic and ensure they know he is free of their idolatry.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r2.anchor: لا أنهم كانوا أهل شهادة، ولكنه نهاية للتقرير أي لتعرفوا

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r3.claim: Hūd declares himself free from worshipping the idols they associate with God.

BURSEVI:v4p92/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92/r1.claim: اعتراك explains an omitted verbal noun: their only statement about Hud is that affliction has overtaken him.
BURSEVI:v4p92/r1.anchor: إلا اعتريك قوله اعتراك جملة مفسرة لمصدر محذوف تقديره ما نقول في شأنك إلا قولنا اعتراك

BURSEVI:v4p92/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92/r2.claim: اعتراك means that something afflicted or struck him; the ب in بسوء is causative.
BURSEVI:v4p92/r2.anchor: قوله اعتراك جملة مفسرة لمصدر محذوف تقديره ما نقول في شأنك إلا قولنا اعتراك أي : أصابك من عراه يعره

BURSEVI:v4p92/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92/r3.claim: They allege that some idols afflicted Hud with madness as revenge for his insulting them and deterring people from their worship.
BURSEVI:v4p92/r3.anchor: أي : بجنون لسبك إياها وصدك عنها وعداوتك مكافأة لك منها على سوء فعلك بسوء الجزاء

BURSEVI:v4p92/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92/r4.claim: Hud means I call you to witness, avoiding coordination of an imperative construction with a declarative one.
BURSEVI:v4p92/r4.anchor: قال هود إني أشهد الله واشهدوا أي : وأقول أشهدوا لئلا يلزم عطف الإنشاء على الخبر أني بريىء

BURSEVI:v4p92/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92/r5.claim: The shared complement أني بريء is governed by both أشهد الله and اشهدوا.
BURSEVI:v4p92/r5.anchor: تنازع فيه أشهد الله واشهدوا أي : على أني برييء مما تشركون أي : من إشراككم.

BURSEVI:v4p92/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92/r6.claim: Hud truly calls God as witness but calls his hostile people to witness sarcastically, showing contempt for their hostility.
BURSEVI:v4p92/r6.anchor: وإشهاد الله تعالى حقيقة ، وإشهادهم استهزاء بهم واستهانة ، إذ لا يقول أحد لمن يعاديه أشهدك على أني بريء

BURSEVI:v4p92/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92/r7.claim: من دونه can explain the phrase as associating partners besides God; alternatively, ما is a relative pronoun referring to what they associate.
BURSEVI:v4p92/r7.anchor: من دونه أي : من دون الله أو مما تشركون من آلهة غير الله فما موصولة وإشهاد الله تعالى حقيقة

BURSEVI:v4p92/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92/r8.claim: Since they call idols gods and claim they can harm him, Hud first repudiates their divinity, then challenges them to harm him.
BURSEVI:v4p92/r8.anchor: واعلم أنهم لما سموا أصنامهم آلهة وأثبتوا لها الضرر نفى هود بقوله إني أشهد الله الآية كونهم آلهة رأسا ثم نفى الضرر

BURSEVI:v4p92/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92/r9.claim: كيد means secretly intending harm; for humans it is a malicious scheme, while God's kيد is just planning requital for deeds.
BURSEVI:v4p92/r9.anchor: الكيد إرادة مضرة الغير خفية وهو من الخلق الحيلة السيئة ، ومن الله التدبير بالحق لمجازاة أعمال الخلق

BURSEVI:v4p92/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92/r10.claim: The phrase فكونوا أنتم وآلهتكم جميعا is circumstantial, attached to the pronoun in كيدوني.
BURSEVI:v4p92/r10.anchor: فكونوا أنتم وآلهتكم جميعا حال من ضمير كيدوني على قصد إهلاكي بكل طريق.

BURSEVI:v4p92/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92/r11.claim: Hud tells them not to delay, spare, or grant him any respite.
BURSEVI:v4p92/r11.anchor: ثم لا تنظرون لا تمهلوني ولا تسامحوني في ذلك فالفاء لتفريع الأمر على زعمهم في قدرة آلهتهم

BURSEVI:v4p92/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92/r12.claim: The ف makes the challenge follow from both their claim that idols can harm him and his repudiation of them.
BURSEVI:v4p92/r12.anchor: فالفاء لتفريع الأمر على زعمهم في قدرة آلهتهم على ما قالوا : وعلى البراءة كليهما كما في الإرشاد.

BURSEVI:v4p92/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92/r13.claim: The soul and its traits, Satan, desire, and the world ceaselessly plot against the heart, but divine support makes the heart immune to their plot.
BURSEVI:v4p92/r13.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن النفس وصفاتها والشيطان والهوى والدنيا في كيد القلب على الدوام والقلب المؤيد بالتأييد الرباني لا يناله كيدهم

RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r5.claim: The verb iʿtarā means that something came over or afflicted someone.

RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r6.claim: They claimed that because Hūd insulted their gods, one had made him mad and ruined his mind.
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r6.anchor: أنك شتمت آلهتنا فجعلتك مجنونا وأفسدت عقلك

RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r7.claim: Hūd calls God and his opponents as witnesses that he disavows what they associate with God.
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r7.anchor: إنى أشهد الله واشهدوا أنى برىء مما تشركون
